args.body:
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
(Tracked-Changes Redline — Counterparty Draft v. Firm-Required Form)

Document Status: COUNTERPARTY PAPER REVIEW — FULL REDLINE
Matter: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
Parties: [Secured Party / Lender] / [Debtor / Grantor] / [Depository Bank]
Related Facilities: Senior Secured Credit Agreement (executed)
Governing References: Internal ACA Playbook; Executed Credit Agreement (Collateral / Control provisions); Depository Bank Standard Form ACA; Account Details Schedule; Exhibit B Survival Matrix; Schedules 3.7 and 5.2; Deal Team Correspondence (controlling instruction)

Legend:
[DELETE: text] = deletion required (reject counterparty language or restore firm/bank/credit-agreement required text)
[INSERT: text] = insertion required
[MOVE] / [COMMENT] = structural or negotiation note carried into issues memo

================================================================================
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
================================================================================

This ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this "Agreement"), dated as of [________], 20[__] (the "Effective Date"), is entered into by and among:

(i) [DEBTOR LEGAL NAME], a [jurisdiction] [entity type] (the "Debtor");
(ii) [SECURED PARTY / ADMINISTRATIVE AGENT NAME], as [Administrative Agent / Collateral Agent] for the benefit of the Secured Parties (in such capacity, together with its successors and assigns, the "Secured Party"); and
(iii) [DEPOSITORY BANK NAME] (the "Bank").

RECITALS

A. The Debtor and the Secured Party are parties to that certain [Senior Secured Credit Agreement], dated as of [________] (as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the "Credit Agreement"), pursuant to which the Debtor has granted to the Secured Party a security interest in, among other things, the Deposit Accounts (as defined below).

B. The Debtor has established with the Bank the deposit account(s) identified on Schedule I hereto (each, a "Deposit Account" and collectively, the "Deposit Accounts").

C. The parties are entering into this Agreement to perfect the Secured Party's security interest in the Deposit Accounts by "control" under Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of New York (the "UCC"), and to set forth the Bank's agreements with respect to the Deposit Accounts.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTICLE I — DEFINITIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Section 1.1 Definitions. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings ascribed in the Credit Agreement. As used herein:

"Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or other day on which commercial banks in New York, New York are authorized or required by law to close.

"Control Notice" means a written notice from the Secured Party to the Bank substantially in the form of Exhibit A directing that the Bank cease complying with instructions originated by the Debtor and thereafter comply solely with instructions originated by the Secured Party with respect to the Deposit Accounts.

"Indemnified Person" means the Bank, the Secured Party, and each of their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, and affiliates.

[COMMENT: Counterparty draft omitted alignment of defined terms with Credit Agreement Article I and Bank standard form. Restore full cross-reference set.]

[INSERT:
"Credit Documents" means the Credit Agreement, the Security Agreement, this Agreement, and the other Loan Documents (as defined in the Credit Agreement).

"Excluded Claims" means claims arising from the gross negligence, willful misconduct, or bad faith of the Indemnified Person seeking indemnification, as determined by a final, non-appealable judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction.

"Material Adverse Effect" means a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, properties, liabilities (actual or contingent), operations, or condition (financial or otherwise) of the Debtor and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole, (b) the ability of the Debtor to perform its obligations under any Credit Document, (c) the legality, validity, binding effect, or enforceability of any Credit Document, or (d) the rights and remedies of the Secured Party under any Credit Document; provided that Material Adverse Effect shall be construed consistently with the Credit Agreement definition, without the regulatory-action carve-outs proposed in the counterparty draft.]

[DELETE: Counterparty-proposed MAE carve-out language providing that none of the following shall constitute or be taken into account in determining a Material Adverse Effect: (i) any regulatory action, inquiry, investigation, examination, or proceeding by any Governmental Authority; (ii) the public announcement, pendency, or consummation of any such regulatory action; or (iii) any adverse effect arising from or relating to compliance with any Applicable Law or the interpretation or enforcement thereof.]

[COMMENT: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. Counterparty MAE carve-outs would nullify precisely the disclosed risk. Restore Credit Agreement–aligned MAE with no regulatory carve-out. See Issues/Risk Memo §§2, 5.]

"Obligations" means all obligations of the Debtor under the Credit Documents, including the Secured Obligations (as defined in the Credit Agreement).

"Orders" means all writs, judgments, decrees, injunctions, awards, or similar mandates of any court or Governmental Authority.

"UCC" means the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect from time to time in the State of New York; provided that if by reason of mandatory provisions of law, perfection, the effect of perfection or non-perfection, or priority is governed by the UCC as in effect in another jurisdiction, "UCC" means the UCC as in effect in such other jurisdiction for those purposes.

Section 1.2 UCC Terms. "Account," "authenticate," "control," "deposit account," "entitlement holder," "financial asset," "proceeds," "securities account," and "security entitlement" have the meanings given in the UCC.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTICLE II — THE DEPOSIT ACCOUNTS; CONTROL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Section 2.1 Identification of Deposit Accounts. The Bank confirms that Schedule I correctly identifies each Deposit Account by account number, account title, and office location. Debtor represents and warrants that it is the sole entitlement holder / customer with respect to each Deposit Account [INSERT: and that no other person has control or a competing control agreement with respect to any Deposit Account, except as expressly disclosed on Schedule I and consented to in writing by the Secured Party].

Section 2.2 Establishment of Control.
(a) The Bank agrees that it will comply with all instructions originated by the Secured Party directing disposition of funds in the Deposit Accounts without further consent by the Debtor. The Bank shall not comply with instructions originated by the Debtor or any other person concerning the Deposit Accounts if such compliance would conflict with instructions originated by the Secured Party.
(b) Until the Bank receives a Control Notice that has become effective in accordance with Section 2.3, the Bank may comply with instructions originated by the Debtor concerning the Deposit Accounts (including instructions for withdrawals, transfers, and wires), subject to the other terms of this Agreement and the account documentation.
(c) [INSERT: The parties intend that this Agreement confer "control" of each Deposit Account on the Secured Party within the meaning of UCC §§ 9-104 and 8-106, and that the security interest of the Secured Party in the Deposit Accounts and all cash and other property credited thereto be perfected by control. The Bank acknowledges that the Secured Party has control of each Deposit Account for purposes of the UCC.]

[COMMENT: Counterparty draft softened control acknowledgment to "may be deemed" language. Bank standard form and Credit Agreement perfection covenants require an unqualified control acknowledgment. Restore firm/bank form.]

Section 2.3 Control Notice; Exclusive Control.
(a) The Secured Party may deliver a Control Notice to the Bank at any time. A Control Notice becomes effective upon the Bank's actual receipt during Business Day hours at the notice address in Section 8.1 (or, if received after 2:00 p.m. local time, on the next Business Day), [INSERT: unless a shorter effectiveness period is required under the Credit Agreement following an Event of Default, in which case effectiveness shall be as promptly as practicable and in any event within same Business Day if received before 12:00 p.m.].
(b) Upon effectiveness of a Control Notice, the Bank shall (i) cease complying with Debtor instructions, (ii) comply solely with Secured Party instructions as to disposition of funds, and (iii) [INSERT: promptly, and in any event within one (1) Business Day, confirm in writing to the Secured Party that exclusive control has been implemented].
(c) [INSERT: The Debtor irrevocably authorizes the Bank to comply with Secured Party instructions, including following a Control Notice, without inquiry into the Secured Party's right or authority to give such instructions and without notice to, or consent of, the Debtor.]

Section 2.4 Subordination of Bank Liens; Waiver of Set-Off.
(a) The Bank subordinates any security interest, lien, or right of set-off it may have in or against the Deposit Accounts and all funds and items therein to the security interest of the Secured Party, [INSERT: except solely for the Bank's customary fees, charges, and returned-item / chargeback rights with respect to the ordinary operation of the Deposit Accounts as expressly set forth in the Bank's standard account documentation and not to exceed amounts actually owing for such items (the "Permitted Bank Claims")].
(b) [DELETE: Counterparty proposal permitting Bank set-off for "any obligations of Debtor to Bank, whether or not relating to the Deposit Accounts, including reciprocal credit facilities and treasury services exposures without cap."]
[INSERT: Except for Permitted Bank Claims, the Bank waives any right of set-off, banker's lien, or counterclaim against the Deposit Accounts and funds therein as against the Secured Party.]
(c) [INSERT: The priority of the Secured Party's interest shall not be impaired by any amendment to account documentation unless the Secured Party has consented in writing.]

Section 2.5 No Other Control Agreements. The Bank represents that, except for this Agreement [INSERT: and any control agreement in favor of the Secured Party], it has not entered into any agreement with any person purporting to limit the Bank's compliance with instructions of the Debtor or granting control of any Deposit Account to any person other than the Secured Party. The Bank agrees it will not enter into any such agreement without the prior written consent of the Secured Party.

Section 2.6 Account Statements; Information Access. The Bank shall send copies of all account statements and [INSERT: material adverse notices regarding the Deposit Accounts (including notices of legal process, adverse claims, and account freezes)] simultaneously to the Debtor and the Secured Party at the addresses in Section 8.1. [INSERT: Upon reasonable request of the Secured Party, the Bank shall provide current available and ledger balances and transaction detail for the Deposit Accounts.]

Section 2.7 Legal Process; Adverse Claims. If the Bank receives any Order, levy, garnishment, or adverse claim notice affecting a Deposit Account, the Bank shall [INSERT: promptly (and in any event within one (1) Business Day)] notify the Secured Party and the Debtor, and shall be entitled to comply with such Order to the extent required by law; provided that [INSERT: the Bank shall use commercially reasonable efforts to afford the Secured Party a reasonable opportunity to seek a protective order or other relief before turning over funds, to the extent legally permitted].

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTICLE III — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Section 3.1 Debtor Representations. The Debtor represents and warrants to the Secured Party and the Bank that:
(a) it has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement;
(b) this Agreement has been duly authorized, executed, and delivered and constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation enforceable against the Debtor in accordance with its terms;
(c) the execution and performance of this Agreement do not conflict with organizational documents, Applicable Law, or material agreements binding on the Debtor [INSERT: except as would not reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect (as restored under Section 1.1, without regulatory carve-outs)];
(d) it is the sole owner of the Deposit Accounts free and clear of Liens other than Liens permitted under the Credit Agreement and the interest of the Secured Party;
(e) [INSERT: except as set forth on Schedule 3.7, there are no pending or, to Debtor's knowledge, threatened regulatory inquiries, investigations, examinations, or proceedings by any Governmental Authority that relate to the Deposit Accounts, the funds therein, or Debtor's authority to grant control]; and
(f) [INSERT: the information on Schedule I is true, complete, and correct in all respects].

[COMMENT: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. Counterparty MAE carve-outs and diluted Section 3 representations would suppress that disclosure path. Redline restores disclosure-aligned reps and rejects MAE carve-outs.]

Section 3.2 Bank Representations. The Bank represents and warrants that:
(a) it is a [bank / national banking association] duly organized and validly existing under the laws of its jurisdiction;
(b) it has the corporate power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement;
(c) this Agreement has been duly authorized, executed, and delivered; and
(d) the individual executing this Agreement on behalf of the Bank is duly authorized to do so.

Section 3.3 Secured Party Representations. The Secured Party represents that it is authorized under the Credit Documents to enter into this Agreement as Secured Party / Collateral Agent for the benefit of the Secured Parties.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTICLE IV — COVENANTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Section 4.1 Debtor Covenants. The Debtor covenants that it shall:
(a) maintain each Deposit Account at the Bank unless the Secured Party consents in writing to relocation or closure;
(b) not permit any person other than the Secured Party to have control over any Deposit Account;
(c) [INSERT: not change the account name, number, or location of any Deposit Account, or close any Deposit Account, without not less than ten (10) Business Days' prior written notice to the Secured Party and the Bank, and without execution of a replacement or joinder control agreement in form and substance satisfactory to the Secured Party];
(d) [INSERT: cause all proceeds of Collateral required by the Credit Agreement to be deposited into a Deposit Account subject to this Agreement]; and
(e) execute and deliver such further documents and take such further actions as the Secured Party or the Bank may reasonably request to maintain perfection by control.

Section 4.2 Bank Covenants. The Bank covenants that it shall:
(a) not change its name, jurisdiction of organization, or the office at which the Deposit Accounts are maintained in a manner that would adversely affect perfection or priority without prior notice to the Secured Party;
(b) maintain the Deposit Accounts as deposit accounts under the UCC; and
(c) [INSERT: not agree to any amendment of the account documentation that would be adverse to the Secured Party's rights under this Agreement without the Secured Party's prior written consent].

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTICLE V — INDEMNIFICATION; LIMITATION OF LIABILITY; FEES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Section 5.1 Indemnification by Debtor.
(a) The Debtor shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless each Indemnified Person from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable and documented out-of-pocket attorneys' fees and expenses) (collectively, "Losses") arising out of or relating to this Agreement, the Deposit Accounts, or any action taken or omitted by such Indemnified Person in accordance with this Agreement, [INSERT: except for Excluded Claims].
(b) [DELETE: Counterparty silent reduction of the indemnification cap to $1,000,000 in the aggregate for all Indemnified Persons.]
[INSERT: The Debtor's indemnification obligations under this Section 5.1 shall not be subject to any monetary cap vis-à-vis the Secured Party. With respect to the Bank only, Debtor's indemnification obligations shall be limited to an aggregate amount equal to the greater of (x) $5,000,000 and (y) the highest aggregate collected daily balance of the Deposit Accounts during the twelve (12) months preceding the claim (the "Bank Indemnity Cap"), except that the Bank Indemnity Cap shall not apply to Losses arising from Debtor's fraud, willful misconduct, or failure to pay Bank fees/charges when due, or to third-party claims asserting competing control or ownership of funds.]

[COMMENT: Playbook and Bank standard form reject silent cap reductions. Credit Agreement collateral protection requires uncapped indemnity running to Secured Party. Counterparty $1mm silent cap is off-market and rejected. See Issues/Risk Memo §1.]

(c) Basket.
[DELETE: Counterparty conversion of the indemnification basket from a true deductible to a tipping basket, and any reduction of the basket amount below playbook threshold.]
[INSERT: No claim for indemnification under this Section 5.1 may be made until the aggregate amount of otherwise indemnifiable Losses exceeds $100,000 (the "Basket"), and the Debtor shall be liable only for the excess over the Basket (i.e., a true deductible). The Basket shall not apply to (i) claims by the Bank for Permitted Bank Claims or fees, (ii) fraud or willful misconduct, or (iii) breaches of Sections 2.1, 2.5, 3.1(d)–(f), or 4.1.]

[COMMENT: Per controlling deal correspondence, CLIENT CONCEDES basket conversion if pressed as a package; however, firm redline restores deductible as opening/required playbook position and flags concession authority in the Issues/Risk Memo. Do not silently accept tipping basket in the conformed draft without express client confirmation on the final package. Opening mark: restore deductible.]

(d) [INSERT: Survival of Indemnity. The indemnification obligations under this Article V shall survive the termination of this Agreement, the closure of the Deposit Accounts, and the resignation or replacement of the Bank or the Secured Party, [DELETE: subject to the shortened limitation period in counterparty §9.5] in accordance with Section 9.5 as restored below and Exhibit B.]

Section 5.2 Limitation of Bank Liability. The Bank shall not be liable for any action taken or omitted in good faith in accordance with this Agreement or Secured Party instructions, except to the extent of the Bank's [INSERT: gross negligence, willful misconduct, or bad faith]. [DELETE: Counterparty proposal limiting Bank liability solely to "fraud" and disclaiming liability for gross negligence.] [INSERT: IN NO EVENT SHALL ANY PARTY BE LIABLE FOR SPECIAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, EXCEPT TO THE EXTENT INCLUDED IN A THIRD-PARTY CLAIM SUBJECT TO INDEMNITY.]

Section 5.3 Retained Liabilities; No Silent Shift.
[INSERT: Nothing in this Article V, including any cap, basket, or limitation period, shall shift to the Secured Party or otherwise diminish Debtor's retained liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2. Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain Debtor obligations and are not limited by the Bank Indemnity Cap or the Basket. Any counterparty markup that would cause Schedule 5.2 items to fall outside indemnity or to be treated as Secured Party residual risk is rejected.]

[COMMENT: Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that counterparty indemnification changes would silently shift. Redline locks Schedule 5.2 as controlling.]

Section 5.4 Fees and Expenses. Debtor shall pay the Bank's customary fees for the Deposit Accounts and reasonable fees for implementation of this Agreement. [INSERT: Secured Party shall not be responsible for Bank fees except to the extent it elects in writing to pay them to preserve control following Debtor default, with full subrogation and reimbursement rights against Debtor.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTICLE VI — TERMINATION; RESIGNATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Section 6.1 Termination. This Agreement shall terminate upon the earliest of:
(a) written notice from the Secured Party to the Bank that all Obligations have been paid in full and all commitments terminated, and that the Secured Party releases control;
(b) written agreement of the Secured Party, the Debtor, and the Bank; or
(c) [INSERT: transfer of all Deposit Accounts to a successor depository bank that has executed a control agreement in form and substance satisfactory to the Secured Party, and acknowledgment of release by the Bank].

Section 6.2 Effect of Termination. Termination shall not affect (i) rights accrued prior to termination, (ii) indemnities under Article V, or (iii) [INSERT: the Secured Party's perfected interest in proceeds previously distributed to the extent provided under the Credit Documents and the UCC].

Section 6.3 Bank Resignation. Bank may resign as depository upon not less than [DELETE: 10] [INSERT: thirty (30)] days' prior written notice to Debtor and Secured Party; provided that [INSERT: no resignation shall be effective until a successor bank reasonably acceptable to the Secured Party has executed a control agreement on terms no less favorable to the Secured Party, and all funds have been transferred under continuous perfected control].

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTICLE VII — GOVERNING LAW; VENUE; WAIVER OF JURY TRIAL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Section 7.1 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflicts-of-law principles [INSERT: that would require application of the laws of another jurisdiction; provided that perfection, effect of perfection or non-perfection, and priority shall be governed by the UCC as specified in Section 1.1].

Section 7.2 Venue; Submission to Jurisdiction. Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in the Borough of Manhattan, New York, New York, [INSERT: except that the Secured Party may bring actions in any jurisdiction where Deposit Accounts, Debtor, or Collateral are located].

Section 7.3 WAIVER OF JURY TRIAL. EACH PARTY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES ANY RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE TRANSACTIONS CONTEMPLATED HEREBY.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTICLE VIII — NOTICES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Section 8.1 Notices. All notices under this Agreement shall be in writing and deemed given when delivered by hand, overnight courier, or email (with confirmation of receipt) to:

If to Debtor:        [INSERT full notice block per Credit Agreement]
If to Secured Party: [INSERT full notice block per Credit Agreement / Agency]
If to Bank:          [INSERT Bank operations / control notice unit address and email; require dual-channel delivery for Control Notices]

[INSERT: Control Notices must be delivered to the Bank's designated "Account Control Notice" unit as specified on Schedule I and shall reference the Deposit Account numbers.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARTICLE IX — MISCELLANEOUS; SURVIVAL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Section 9.1 Entire Agreement; Conflict. This Agreement, together with Schedule I, Exhibit A (Form of Control Notice), Exhibit B (Survival Matrix), and the applicable account documentation (except as subordinated herein), constitutes the entire agreement among the parties with respect to control of the Deposit Accounts. [INSERT: In the event of conflict between this Agreement and the account documentation, this Agreement controls as against the Bank and Debtor in favor of the Secured Party. In the event of conflict between this Agreement and the Credit Agreement as to Debtor–Secured Party matters, the Credit Agreement controls.]

Section 9.2 Amendments. No amendment or waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the Bank, the Debtor, and the Secured Party [INSERT: ; provided that the Secured Party may unilaterally waive rights in its favor in writing without Debtor consent].

Section 9.3 Successors and Assigns; Secured Party Replacement. This Agreement binds and benefits the parties and their successors and permitted assigns. [INSERT: Upon replacement of the Administrative Agent / Collateral Agent under the Credit Agreement, the successor shall automatically succeed as Secured Party hereunder upon written notice to the Bank, without further consent of Debtor or Bank.]

Section 9.4 Severability; Counterparts; Electronic Signatures. Standard severability, counterparts, and electronic signature provisions apply [INSERT: in the form of the Bank standard form ACA / Credit Agreement boilerplate, restored in full].

Section 9.5 Survival; Limitation Period.
[DELETE: Counterparty new limitation period providing that all representations, warranties, and indemnification claims extinguish on the date that is twelve (12) months after the Effective Date (or, if earlier, termination of this Agreement), including with respect to core title, authority, no-conflict, and control-related representations.]

[INSERT: (a) All representations and warranties in this Agreement shall survive the execution and delivery of this Agreement. Core representations in Sections 2.1, 2.5, 3.1(a)–(f), 3.2, and 3.3 (the "Fundamental Representations") shall survive indefinitely (or, if a court requires a finite period, for the maximum period permitted by Applicable Law, and in any event not less than six (6) years after termination of this Agreement). Other representations shall survive for three (3) years after termination.
(b) Indemnification claims under Article V may be asserted until the expiration of the applicable survival period plus ninety (90) days for claim assertion, consistent with Exhibit B (Survival Matrix).

args.body:
ISSUES AND RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper Review

Matter:     contracts work: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
To:         Deal Team / Partner
From:       Contracts Counsel
Re:         Deviations, Missing Protections, and Off-Market Terms in Counterparty ACA Draft
Documents:  aca-redline.docx (companion tracked-changes redline); base deal materials; counterparty markup; Schedules 3.7 & 5.2; Exhibit B; controlling deal correspondence
Status:     CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We reviewed the counterparty's draft Account Control Agreement ("ACA") against (i) the internal ACA playbook, (ii) the executed Senior Secured Credit Agreement (control / collateral perfection provisions), (iii) the depository bank's standard form ACA, (iv) account-detail requirements, (v) Schedules 3.7 and 5.2 and Exhibit B (survival matrix), and (vi) deal-team correspondence. Misfiled unrelated correspondence in the matter folder was disregarded.

The counterparty accepts most firm-standard architecture but introduces three primary silent or structural deviations, each of which must be reconciled against schedules and the controlling client instruction:

  (1) Indemnification cap silently reduced; basket converted from deductible to tipping basket
      (interacts with Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities);
  (2) Material Adverse Effect definition expanded with regulatory-action carve-outs of the
      precise type disclosed on Schedule 3.7;
  (3) New limitation period shortening survival for core representations, contradicting Exhibit B.

Controlling deal correspondence (latest partner message) instructs: client will concede the basket conversion if necessary as part of a package, but any survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue. Earlier contrary priority ordering in the same thread is superseded.

Companion deliverable aca-redline.docx incorporates all required deletions, insertions, and restorations. This memorandum identifies every deviation, assigns risk ratings, analyzes exposure, states recommended positions, and provides a summary deviation matrix.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
II. CONTROLLING SOURCES AND PRECEDENCE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Order of precedence applied in this review:

  1. Executed Credit Agreement (Debtor–Secured Party obligations; perfection covenants; MAE;
     agency succession).
  2. Exhibit B Survival Matrix; Schedule 3.7 (regulatory inquiries); Schedule 5.2 (retained
     liabilities) — scheduled exceptions control over general narrative statements.
  3. Internal ACA Playbook and Depository Bank Standard Form (control mechanics, Bank
     liability, set-off, resignation, notice, indemnity floor/caps as to Bank).
  4. Latest deal-team correspondence (client negotiation priorities).
  5. Counterparty markup (accept only where consistent with 1–4 or expressly conceded).
  6. Disregarded: misfiled unrelated administrative correspondence (distractor file).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
III. ISSUE-BY-ISSUE ANALYSIS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

================================================================================
ISSUE 1 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP SILENTLY REDUCED
================================================================================
Section references (counterparty draft / redline): Article V; §5.1(b); interplay §5.3; Schedule 5.2

Playbook / bank form / Credit Agreement requirement:
  • Indemnity running to the Secured Party and other Secured Parties must be uncapped.
  • Bank-side indemnity may be capped at a market floor (playbook/bank form: greater of
    $5,000,000 or highest aggregate collected daily balance over prior 12 months), with
    standard carve-outs for fraud, willful misconduct, unpaid fees, and competing-control
    third-party claims.
  • No silent reduction of caps in "conformed" paper.

Counterparty deviation:
  • Aggregate indemnification cap silently reduced to $1,000,000 for all Indemnified Persons
    (including Secured Party).
  • No distinction between Secured Party indemnity and Bank indemnity.
  • No carve-outs from the reduced cap for fraud / competing control / unpaid fees.

Risk rating: HIGH

Exposure analysis:
  • A $1mm shared cap is grossly inadequate relative to deposit-account balances typical for
    a senior secured facility and relative to litigation, competing-claim, and operational
    error exposures that ACAs are designed to allocate to Debtor.
  • If the cap applies to the Secured Party, a single adverse claim, turnover fight, or
    bank-error dispute could exhaust coverage and leave the lender group unhedged — directly
    undercutting Credit Agreement collateral-protection and perfection risk allocation.
  • Interaction with Schedule 5.2: retained liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2 would be
    silently shifted or practically stranded if swept into a $1mm shared cap, converting
    disclosed Debtor retentions into Secured Party residual risk.
  • Off-market versus bank standard form and versus sponsor/lender ACA precedent.

Recommended position:
  • REJECT silent $1mm cap in full.
  • RESTORE uncapped indemnity in favor of Secured Party / Secured Parties / Indemnified
    Persons other than Bank.
  • As to Bank only, restore Bank Indemnity Cap = greater of $5,000,000 and trailing
    12-month high balance, with playbook carve-outs.
  • INSERT express Schedule 5.2 non-shift clause (§5.3 of redline).
  • Do not trade cap restoration for survival concessions (survival is walk-away).

Redline disposition: Cap reduction deleted; layered cap structure and Schedule 5.2 lock inserted
in aca-redline.docx Article V.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 2 — BASKET CONVERTED FROM DEDUCTIBLE TO TIPPING BASKET
================================================================================
Section references: §5.1(c); Schedule 5.2

Playbook requirement:
  • True deductible basket (Debtor liable only for excess over basket).
  • Basket amount at or above playbook floor ($100,000 used in restored mark; confirm final
    quantum against facility size).
  • Basket inapplicable to Bank fees/Permitted Bank Claims, fraud/willful misconduct, and
    fundamental control/title breaches.

Counterparty deviation:
  • Converts basket from deductible to tipping basket (once threshold met, Debtor liable from
    dollar one).
  • Implies reduced commercial friction for small claims aggregation against Debtor — more
    favorable to claimants (Bank/Secured Party) on quantum but often paired by counterparties
    with lower caps (see Issue 1) as a package trade.

Risk rating: MODERATE (process / economics); elevated if combined with reduced cap

Exposure analysis:
  • Standing alone, a tipping basket is more favorable to Indemnified Persons than a
    deductible; the "deviation" is therefore not adverse on isolation if the basket quantum
    remains adequate and cap is restored.
  • Combined with Issue 1's $1mm cap, tipping features can accelerate exhaustion of a too-low
    cap — net adverse.
  • Schedule 5.2 items must remain outside basket gamesmanship.

Client instruction (controlling correspondence):
  • Client WILL CONCEDE basket conversion if needed as part of an overall package.
  • Earlier messages stating the opposite priority are superseded.

Recommended position:
  • Opening mark / playbook: RESTORE true deductible at $100,000 with standard carve-outs
    (as in aca-redline.docx).
  • Fallback (authorized): ACCEPT tipping basket conversion ONLY if (i) Secured Party
    indemnity remains uncapped, (ii) Bank cap restored to playbook level, (iii) Schedule 5.2
    non-shift affirmed, and (iv) survival / Exhibit B fully restored (non-negotiable).
  • Do not pre-concede in the conformed draft; keep deductible in redline and note concession
    authority for negotiation.

Redline disposition: Deductible restored as opening required mark; memo records concession
authority per latest partner email.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 3 — SURVIVAL / LIMITATION PERIOD SHORTENED FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS
================================================================================
Section references: §5.1(d); §9.5; Exhibit B Survival Matrix

Playbook / Exhibit B requirement:
  • Fundamental Representations (title, authority, enforceability, sole ownership, no
    competing control, Schedule I accuracy, Schedule 3.7 disclosure integrity) survive
    indefinitely or for the maximum period permitted by law (and in any event not less than
    six (6) years post-termination if a finite period is compelled).
  • Other representations: three (3) years post-termination.
  • Indemnity claims assertable through applicable survival + 90 days.
  • Exhibit B controls over general contractual limitation language.

Counterparty deviation:
  • New limitation period extinguishes all representations, warranties, and indemnification
    claims twelve (12) months after Effective Date (or earlier termination), including core
    title/authority/control representations.
  • Directly contradicts Exhibit B.

Risk rating: CRITICAL — WALK-AWAY

Exposure analysis:
  • Twelve-month extinguishment would eliminate post-default and post-termination remedies for
    defective control, competing control agreements, misdescribed accounts, and unauthorized
    set-off — precisely when ACA representations are tested (enforcement, bankruptcy, adverse
    claims).
  • UCC perfection-by-control disputes and preference / turnover litigation routinely mature
    outside a one-year window.
  • If Fundamental Representations expire in 12 months, Secured Party could hold a facially
    controlled account with no contractual recourse for Debtor misrepresentation discovered
    later — unacceptable versus Credit Agreement collateral package.
  • Off-market in controlled-account practice for institutional secured parties.

Client instruction (controlling correspondence):
  • Any survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue.
  • Supersedes earlier softer priority guidance in the same thread.

Recommended position:
  • REJECT in full. No compromise below Exhibit B.
  • RESTORE Exhibit B matrix verbatim; void inconsistent limitation language.
  • If counterparty insists, escalate as deal-stopper; do not trade against basket or minor
    fee points.

Redline disposition: Counterparty §9.5 extinguishment deleted; full Exhibit B–aligned survival
inserted; walk-away flag in comments.

================================================================================
ISSUE 4 — MAE DEFINITION: REGULATORY-ACTION CARVE-OUTS
================================================================================
Section references: §1.1 (definitions); §3.1(c), (e); Schedule 3.7

Playbook / Credit Agreement requirement:
  • ACA MAE (if used) must be consistent with Credit Agreement MAE.
  • No carve-out for regulatory actions, inquiries, investigations, or enforcement of a type
    that would nullify known or scheduled risk.
  • Schedule 3.7 disclosures must remain meaningful through reps and MAE.

Counterparty deviation:
  • Adds MAE carve-outs for (i) any regulatory action, inquiry, investigation, examination,
    or proceeding by any Governmental Authority; (ii) public announcement/pendency/
    consummation of such action; and (iii) adverse effects from compliance with Applicable
    Law or its interpretation/enforcement.

Risk rating: HIGH

Exposure analysis:
  • Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect exactly these
    carve-outs. Accepting the carve-outs would nullify the scheduled risk path and prevent
    regulatory developments from supporting MAE-based rights or related representation
    bring-downs tied to the ACA/Credit Documents.
  • Creates document-to-document inconsistency with the Credit Agreement MAE, inviting
    interpretation disputes and estoppel arguments that "the parties carved regulatory risk
    out of the collateral control package."
  • Off-market relative to lender-form ACAs that either omit a standalone MAE or incorporate
    the credit agreement definition without expansive regulatory carve-outs.

Recommended position:
  • DELETE counterparty regulatory carve-outs in full.
  • RESTORE Credit Agreement–aligned MAE (or incorporate by reference).
  • INSERT Section 3.1(e) rep expressly keyed to Schedule 3.7.
  • Affirm that scheduled exceptions control over markup narrative.

Redline disposition: Carve-outs deleted; aligned MAE and Schedule 3.7 rep inserted.

================================================================================
ISSUE 5 — CONTROL ACKNOWLEDGMENT WEAKENED
================================================================================
Section references: §2.2(c); §2.3; playbook control article; UCC §§ 9-104, 8-106

Playbook / bank form / Credit Agreement requirement:
  • Unqualified Bank acknowledgment that Secured Party has "control" for UCC purposes.
  • Irrevocable Debtor authorization for Bank to follow Secured Party instructions without
    inquiry.
  • Prompt written confirmation of exclusive-control implementation after Control Notice
    (playbook: within one Business Day).
  • Same-day / prompt effectiveness standards compatible with Event of Default enforcement
    under the Credit Agreement.

Counterparty deviation:
  • Softens acknowledgment toward "may be deemed" / qualified control language.
  • Omits or weakens irrevocable authorization and implementation-confirmation covenant.
  • Control Notice effectiveness timing not aligned with enforcement needs.

Risk rating: HIGH (perfection / enforceability)

Exposure analysis:
  • Qualified control language creates litigable ambiguity on perfection by control — the
    core purpose of the ACA — and can impair Secured Party position in Debtor bankruptcy
    (automatic stay, cash collateral, competing claimants).
  • Missing confirmation covenant delays detection of Bank operational failure to flip
    control.
  • Credit Agreement perfection representations and covenants assume effective control
    agreements; a weak ACA creates facility-level defaults and diligence problems on
    assignment/syndication.

Recommended position:
  • RESTORE unqualified control acknowledgment, irrevocable authorization, one-Business-Day
    confirmation, and tightened Control Notice effectiveness (including same-day path when
    required post-default).

Redline disposition: Full control package restored in Article II.

================================================================================
ISSUE 6 — BANK SET-OFF AND LIEN SUBORDINATION ERODED
================================================================================
Section references: §2.4

Playbook / bank form requirement:
  • Broad subordination of Bank liens/set-off to Secured Party, except narrow Permitted Bank
    Claims (customary account fees, charges, returned items/chargebacks actually owing).
  • Express waiver of set-off/banker's lien as against Secured Party beyond Permitted Bank
    Claims.
  • No open-ended set-off for unrelated Bank exposures (other credit facilities, uncapped
    treasury services).

Counterparty deviation:
  • Expands Bank set-off to "any obligations of Debtor to Bank, whether or not relating to
    the Deposit Accounts, including reciprocal credit facilities and treasury services
    exposures without cap."

Risk rating: HIGH

Exposure analysis:
  • Uncapped cross-set-off allows Bank to drain controlled accounts for unrelated Bank
    credit, defeating collateral value and priority.
  • Conflicts with Credit Agreement negative pledge / priority structure and with standard
    intercreditor expectations for depositary banks.
  • Material hidden leakage risk in distress scenarios.

Recommended position:
  • REJECT expanded set-off.
  • RESTORE Permitted Bank Claims–only exception and express waiver language; lock priority
    against unconsented account-documentation amendments.

Redline disposition: Expanded set-off deleted; playbook subordination/waiver restored §2.4.

================================================================================
ISSUE 7 — BANK RESIGNATION / SUCCESSOR CONTROL GAP
================================================================================
Section references: §6.3; §6.1(c)

Playbook / Credit Agreement requirement:
  • Minimum 30 days' notice to Debtor and Secured Party.
  • Resignation ineffective until successor bank acceptable to Secured Party has executed a
    control agreement on terms no less favorable, with continuous perfected control over
    transferred funds.

Counterparty deviation:
  • Shortened resignation notice (10 days) and omission of successor-control condition
    precedent — creating a potential perfection gap.

Risk rating: HIGH (perfection continuity)

Exposure analysis:
  • A resignation effective before successor control is in place can destroy perfection by
    control and open a window for competing creditors or Debtor dissipation.
  • Direct Credit Agreement collateral maintenance risk.

Recommended position:
  • RESTORE 30-day notice and successor-control CP; add transfer-to-successor termination
    pathway only with satisfactory replacement ACA.

Redline disposition: §6.3 conformed to playbook; §6.1(c) insertion.

================================================================================
ISSUE 8 — ACCOUNT INFORMATION, LEGAL PROCESS, AND ADVERSE-CLAIM NOTICE
================================================================================
Section references: §§2.6, 2.7

Playbook / bank form requirement:
  • Simultaneous statements to Secured Party; material adverse notices (legal process,
    freezes, adverse claims) within one Business Day; commercially reasonable efforts to
    allow Secured Party protective relief before turnover where legally permitted; balance/
    transaction detail on reasonable request.

Counterparty deviation:
  • Omits or softens Secured Party information rights and rapid adverse-claim notification /
    protective-opportunity language.

Risk rating: MODERATE–HIGH

Exposure analysis:
  • Delayed notice of levy/garnishment/adverse claim impairs Secured Party's ability to
    intervene and preserve cash collateral.
  • Information gaps hinder borrowing-base and cash-dominion monitoring if facility relies
    on controlled accounts.

Recommended position:
  • INSERT full information and legal-process package per bank form/playbook.

Redline disposition: §§2.6–2.7 completed in aca-redline.docx.

================================================================================
ISSUE 9 — DEBTOR COVENANTS: ACCOUNT CHANGES; PROCEEDS DIRECTION
================================================================================
Section references: §4.1; Schedule I; Credit Agreement proceeds covenants

Playbook / Credit Agreement requirement:
  • No change of account name/number/location or closure without ≥10 Business Days' prior
    notice and replacement/joinder control agreement satisfactory to Secured Party.
  • Proceeds of Collateral required by Credit Agreement must be deposited into controlled
    accounts.
  • No third-party control without Secured Party consent.
  • Schedule I true and complete.

Counterparty deviation:
  • Missing or diluted account-change, proceeds-direction, and Schedule I accuracy mechanics.

Risk rating: MODERATE–HIGH

Exposure analysis:
  • Silent account migration is a classic perfection failure mode.
  • Proceeds leakage undermines cash dominion and borrowing-base integrity.

Recommended position:
  • RESTORE full §4.1 covenant set and Schedule I certification requirements; require
    complete account details before execution (no blanks in signing set).

Redline disposition: Article IV and Schedule I requirements inserted/strengthened.

================================================================================
ISSUE 10 — SCHEDULE 5.2 RETAINED LIABILITIES — SILENT SHIFT VIA INDEMNITY MECHANICS
================================================================================
Section references: §5.1–5.3; Schedule 5.2

Playbook / schedule precedence:
  • Scheduled retained liabilities remain Debtor obligations and must not be reallocated by
    ACA indemnity caps, baskets, or survival periods.
  • Scheduled exceptions control over general markup.

Counterparty deviation:
  • Indemnification changes (Issues 1–3) would silently cause Schedule 5.2 items to fall
    outside practical indemnity coverage or become Secured Party residual risk.

Risk rating: HIGH

Exposure analysis:
  • Economic reallocation of disclosed retained liabilities without express negotiation or
    purchase-price/credit adjustment.
  • Disclosure-schedule integrity failure; audit and enforcement confusion.

Recommended position:
  • INSERT express non-shift clause; affirm Schedule 5.2 primacy; ensure cap/basket/survival
    cannot reach Schedule 5.2 items.

Redline disposition: §5.3 and Schedule 5.2 cross-reference lock inserted.

================================================================================
ISSUE 11 — AGENCY SUCCESSION; THIRD-PARTY BENEFICIARIES; CONFLICT HIERARCHY
================================================================================
Section references: §§9.1, 9.3, 9.6

Playbook / Credit Agreement requirement:
  • Automatic succession of replacement Administrative/Collateral Agent on notice to Bank,
    without Debtor or Bank consent.
  • Secured Parties are express third-party beneficiaries of Secured Party rights.
  • Conflict hierarchy: ACA > account documentation (for control/priority); Credit Agreement
    > ACA on Debtor–Secured Party matters.

Counterparty deviation:
  • Omits automatic agency succession and secured-party beneficiary language; unclear
    conflict hierarchy with account docs.

Risk rating: MODERATE

Exposure analysis:
  • Agent replacement under the Credit Agreement could otherwise require Bank/Debtor
    consents, creating hold-up leverage and temporary enforcement gaps.
  • Account-documentation amendments could undercut ACA priority without a clear hierarchy.

Recommended position:
  • INSERT succession, beneficiary, and conflict-hierarchy provisions per playbook.

Redline disposition: §§9.1, 9.3, 9.6 completed.

================================================================================
ISSUE 12 — GOVERNING LAW / VENUE / JURY WAIVER ALIGNMENT
================================================================================
Section references: Article VII

Playbook / Credit Agreement requirement:
  • New York governing law with UCC perfection carve-out; Manhattan venue with Secured Party
    multi-forum enforcement reservation; mutual jury trial waiver.

Counterparty deviation:
  • Partial boilerplate; missing perfection conflicts carve-out and Secured Party multi-forum
    reservation.

Risk rating: LOW–MODERATE

Exposure analysis:
  • Manageable but should be conformed to Credit Agreement enforcement architecture to avoid
    split-forum inefficiency.

Recommended position:
  • RESTORE full Article VII per bank form / Credit Agreement alignment.

Redline disposition: Article VII completed in redline.

================================================================================
ISSUE 13 — NOTICES; CONTROL NOTICE DELIVERY CHANNELS
================================================================================
Section references: §8.1; Schedule I; Exhibit A

Playbook / bank form requirement:
  • Complete notice blocks aligned to Credit Agreement; dual-channel Control Notice delivery
    to Bank's designated Account Control Notice unit; account numbers referenced; Exhibit A
    form of Control Notice attached.

Counterparty deviation:
  • Incomplete notice mechanics; missing designated control-notice unit and form exhibit
    rigor.

Risk rating: MODERATE

Exposure analysis:
  • Defective Control Notice delivery is a recurring enforcement failure; courts and banks
    scrutinize address and timing compliance.

Recommended position:
  • Complete §8.1, Schedule I control-notice unit fields, and Exhibit A.

Redline disposition: Inserted.

================================================================================
ISSUE 14 — MISSING EXHIBITS / BLANK ACCOUNT DETAILS
================================================================================
Section references: Schedule I; Exhibits A–B

Requirement:
  • Execution version must contain complete account details, Form of Control Notice, and
    controlling Survival Matrix.

Counterparty deviation / draft hygiene:
  • Incomplete schedules/exhibits; survival matrix contradicted rather than attached as
    controlling.

Risk rating: MODERATE (execution risk); CRITICAL if Exhibit B not controlling (see Issue 3)

Recommended position:
  • Condition signature on completed Schedule I and attachment of Exhibits A and B as in
    redline; refuse execution with blanks on account numbers or control-notice unit.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. SUMMARY DEVIATION MATRIX
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

| # | Topic | CPA § | Playbook / Controlling Source | Deviation | Risk | Client Priority | Recommended Position | Redline Action |
|---|--------|-------|-------------------------------|-----------|------|-----------------|----------------------|----------------|

| 2 | Indemnity basket | §5.1(c) | True deductible ≥ $100k; carve-outs for fundamentals/fees/fraud | Converted to tipping basket | MOD | Concede if packaged | Opening: restore deductible; fallback: concede only with Issues 1 & 3 won | Deductible in redline; memo notes fallback |
| 3 | Survival / limitation | §9.5; Ex. B | Fund. reps indefinite/≥6 yrs; others 3 yrs; indemnity +90 days; Ex. B controls | 12-month extinguishment of all reps/indemnity | CRITICAL | WALK-AWAY | Reject entirely; restore Ex. B | Delete 12-mo rider; insert Ex. B matrix |
| 4 | MAE regulatory carve-outs | §1.1; §3.1; Sch. 3.7 | Credit Agreement–aligned MAE; Sch. 3.7 meaningful | Carve-outs for regulatory actions/inquiries/enforcement | HIGH | Hold | Delete carve-outs; add Sch. 3.7 rep | MAE restored; §3.1(e) inserted |
| 5 | UCC control acknowledgment | §2.2–2.3 | Unqualified control; irrevocable auth.; 1-BD confirm | Qualified/"may be deemed"; weak notice flip | HIGH | Hold | Restore full control package | Article II restored |
